task.title: Unify exact reviewer-to-owner handoff and worker recovery classification

defect_reproduced.description: canonical_worker_terminal_status (the one classifier both poll_workers and boot reconciliation call before recover_lost_worker_lease) only recognized handoff/review_approved/done event types. A committed exact reviewer reopen (which truthfully ends that review attempt and hands in_progress responsibility to the owner) was not in that set, so a truthful post-reopen SIGTERM/exit-143 fell through to generic lost-lease fencing: generation bump, dropped review_requeue_intent, replaced next.
defect_reproduced.reference_example: Registry reviewer run codex-20260906T151222Z-c4a97359 rejected PR5620 head 3f7e9551 at 15:17:07 UTC, generation 19; exact reopen termination at 15:17:18 was followed by lost-lease-bd992815... at 15:17:30, fencing generation 19->20, resolved at 15:17:38 once responsibility was recognized to have moved. See REVIEW_HANDOFF_RECOVERY_RECHECK.md.

fix.change: Added "reopen" to terminal_event_types and to the event-type -> valid task-status map (reopen -> {"in_progress"}), with a role guard requiring expected_role == "reviewer" for a reopen event (mirroring the existing review_approved/handoff/done role guards). All other identity/actor/process-generation/run/queue matching in this function -- already shared by every caller -- applies unchanged.
fix.single_authoritative_classifier: This is the only source change. Both existing call sites in poll_workers (missing_process/lease_expired branch, ~line 10677) and supervisor boot reconciliation (~line 12337) already called canonical_worker_terminal_status before recover_lost_worker_lease, so both now recognize an exact reopen without any call-site-specific policy duplication. owner_worker_canonical_handoff_status (required_role="owner") and active_worker_governance_lease_decision (already reopen-aware for a still-alive worker) are unaffected.
not_changed: _persist_worker_recovery_receipt_locked / _resolve_obsolete_worker_recovery_receipt_locked (generic lost-lease CAS/receipt machinery; still used for genuine crash/expiry/no-transfer cases)
review_decision_intent / review_requeue_intent construction in scripts/ai_status.py command_reopen

reproduced_reopen_sequences.detail: test_missing_process_reviewer_after_exact_reopen_reaps_without_lost_lease (.orchestrator/test_supervisor.py) reproduces the Registry g19-shaped sequence at the poll_workers level: a reviewer worker with a committed exact reopen event, runner_status=failed/exit_code=143/runner_signal=15, missing_process=True. Asserts recover_lost_worker_lease is never called, the worker is marked completed, the queue event is finalized completed, and task.generation is untouched. test_canonical_worker_terminal_status_recognizes_exact_reviewer_reopen exercises the classifier directly, including negative cases: wrong actor, owner-dispatched worker, and required_role="owner" callers must not be satisfied by a reviewer's reopen.

real_two_process_cli_taskstore_outbox_fl.detail: Not implemented in this delivery. The fix and its tests are unit-level (in-process, mocked poll_workers collaborators), matching the existing style of the surrounding suite (e.g. test_live_expired_lease_uses_shared_typed_recovery, test_successful_dead_owner_after_handoff_reaps_without_lost_lease). A real isolated two-process reviewer-runner-exits-after-committed-reopen fixture, and the broader real-process race matrix (reopen/finalize vs recovery/claim/reassign, crash windows around canonical commit/outbox/runner-stop/queue-receipt), were not built. This is the primary residual gap against the full acceptance matrix.

owner_handoff_approve_reject_done_blocke.detail: Existing supervisor/ai_status suites already cover owner handoff, approve, reopen/reject, done, blocker, and reassignment transitions with strict actor/generation/run/queue/PID-ticks/digest/head negatives (unchanged by this fix; full suite reruns below confirm no regression). This delivery adds the reopen-classification-specific positive/negative cases described above; it does not add new coverage for the other listed transitions because their classification paths were not touched.

true_crash_progress_timeout_lease_expiry.detail: recover_lost_worker_lease, review_decision_intent lease-loss handling, and the generic receipt CAS path are untouched by this fix. Full existing regression suites (below) confirm they still fence and recover correctly when no committed reopen/handoff/done/review_approved event matches the worker's exact process identity.

retirement_of_conflicting_classifiers.detail: There was exactly one narrow gap (missing reopen recognition in canonical_worker_terminal_status); no parallel classifier existed to retire. active_worker_governance_lease_decision already handled reopen correctly for a live worker and is unchanged; no old/new dual policy was introduced.

verification.development_failures: Two new tests initially failed with recover_lost_worker_lease called / classifier returning None, because the test fixtures (built by mutating a copy of the shared _owner_worker helper's run_id/queue_event_id) left worker["process_generation"] stale relative to the new identity, so worker_process_identity(worker) returned None and status_event_matches_worker_process failed closed. Fixed by recomputing worker["process_generation"] via worker_process_generation_id(...) after the identity fields were overridden, matching the existing test_reviewer_reopen_ends_the_exact_worker_that_emitted_it pattern. Reran green; failed attempts are not counted in accepted totals.
